title: Back-and-forth: partial isomorphisms and countable structures

based_on.title: Lecture Notes: An Introduction to Model Theory

summary: Build isomorphisms by extending finite matches in both directions, and use countable categoricity to prove completeness.
abstract: When can two countable structures be shown to be isomorphic by matching just a few elements at a time? A back-and-forth construction starts with a finite match preserving both true and false atomic statements and extends it alternately to include an element from each structure, retaining all earlier choices. If suitable extensions are always possible in both directions, the union is an isomorphism. For nonempty countable dense linear orders without endpoints, every finite order-preserving match can be extended this way, so all such orders are isomorphic. This uniqueness also has a consequence for sentences: a satisfiable theory in a countable language with no finite models is complete if all its countably infinite models are isomorphic.
